newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends weak after March expiration.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends weak after March expiration.

text.p: Short covering ahead of its expiration boosted March, but most CME lumber futures contracts ended lower on pressure attributed to the continued slow cash market, traders said.
March expired at $388.90, up $4.30 per tbf, while other months ended $3.40 to $1.00 lower. May finished off most at $363.80 per tbf.
Some early short covering lacked followthrough interest and prices turned lower in quiet dealings prompted by the slow cash trade. Wholesalers continue to discount wood to move product, traders said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $377 per tbf, unchanged from both midweek and week-ago levels. However, there have been reports of spruce trading down to $365 recently, cash sources said.
